method: Extends jump-diffusion modelling to four types of diffusion-triggered jumps (up/down jumps after large up/down diffusion increments) and constructs an equivalent martingale measure via Girsanov plus a normalized Esscher transform.
reason: The paper is entirely a derivation: it states the model under P, changes measure, and derives an explicit no-arbitrage condition linking drift to jump parameters and risk premia. There are no tables, no figures, and no dataset of any kind.

method: Model-based reinforcement learning for controlled diffusions on unbounded state spaces, adaptively partitioning the joint state-action space and refining whenever estimation bias exceeds statistical confidence; establishes regret bounds via a new zooming dimension.
reason: The contribution is regret theory, validated only by numerical experiments on simulated diffusions (including a synthetic multi-asset mean-variance portfolio problem). No real market prices enter anywhere.

method: A deep-learning scheme for McKean-Vlasov FBSDEs with common noise, using Picard iterations plus elicitable scoring functions so conditional statistics (means, quantiles) are learned by an RNN without nested Monte Carlo.
reason: Validation is against closed-form solutions of a systemic-risk interbank model, a quantile-mediated variant, and a non-stationary Aiyagari-Bewley-Huggett growth model. All inputs are simulated; errors are reported as mean Euclidean error versus analytic solutions.

method: Develops a model-free static framework showing absence of static arbitrage across a universe of fixed-income instruments is equivalent to existence of a strictly positive discount curve, then studies least-cost super-replication of liability cash flows including swap-repo strategies.
reason: A theorem paper on cash-flow matrices and price systems with no empirical section, no tables, and no figures. Relevance to Solvency II discounting is discussed but never tested on data.

method: Event study of the high-volume return premium on Korean stocks 2020-2024, splitting abnormal-volume events by investor type (institutional vs retail net buying) and normalizing buying intensity by market capitalization rather than trading value.

method: Derives Merton jump-diffusion dynamics from entropic inference: return symmetry selects log price, continuity plus directionality constraints give the continuous channel, arrival rate plus two jump moments give the jump channel, and the channels factorize; the same principle with no-arbitrage on mean log return selects the Esscher transform.
reason: A derivation paper with no captions, no tables, and no figures in the extracted text. The implied-volatility smile is presented as a consequence of the risk-neutral lognormal mixture, not as a fit to observed option quotes.

method: Maps volatility trajectories into truncated path signatures and trains a gradient boosting classifier to identify which model class (Heston, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck, rough Bergomi, or rough Bergomi at different Hurst values) generated a path.
reason: The paper says explicitly it infers the volatility model from observed (simulated) paths. Every accuracy figure, including the parameter-uncertainty and Heston/OU vol-of-vol misclassification analyses, comes from simulation. No market data is used.

method: Constructs arbitrage-free multi-maturity risk-neutral marginals directly from discrete arbitrage-free option prices, assigning probability mass interval by interval on the observed strike range and completing the distribution with closed-form power-law tails, guaranteeing butterfly- and calendar-arbitrage freeness by construction.

reason: The results are theorems about drift-shift symmetry, steady-state tail exponents and spectral gaps. The single figure shows simulated convergence to a target wealth distribution under different tax structures; no wealth micro-data or market data is fitted.

method: An agent-based market in which one CMA-ES-optimized LSTM institutional agent trades against 20,000 herding retail agents; mean-field reduction maps the system to a nonlinear oscillator exhibiting a Hopf bifurcation in institutional capital and a fold bifurcation in herding scale, and shows square-root price impact is necessary for the limit cycle.
reason: Everything is simulated: the +51% best-of-20-seeds return over 2,000 simulated trading days, the retail imbalance scale, the bifurcation diagrams and the entropy-rate analysis. There is no real price series anywhere in the paper.

method: Derives a closed-form optimal single-horizon holding for an investor with a piecewise-linear budget-threshold utility and exogenous position limits, when returns follow a Generalized Error distribution, interpreting the result as adding a simple risk cost to frictionless trading.
reason: An analytical note. The four figures plot the utility function, the risk scaling function, the risk cost factor versus the kurtosis parameter, and the holding function, all evaluated from the closed forms. The S&P 500 kurtosis value of roughly 0.75 is cited from the author's earlier work, not estimated here, and no backtest or dataset appears.

method: Proposes a cap-axis zero-alpha diagnostic: whole-stock capitalization prefixes paired to equal realized market exposure produce a bridge-alpha curve localizing pricing errors within the market, tested with finite-grid HAC-Gaussian inference and residual-block calibration across 155 factors and six benchmark models.
reason: Built directly on daily CRSP stock returns and Compustat annual fundamentals from January 1967 to December 2024, with a month-end capitalization and dollar-volume screen and delisting-return compounding at the individual stock level. CRSP and Compustat are paid feeds with no free substitute for 1967-onward daily stock-level data.

method: Derives an operational-time variance kernel for the reaction boundary (the zero of a bid-ask imbalance field) in a latent order book via a damped Abel Green-function cumulant, then argues a calendar-time local-volatility projection is admissible only when the forward density and backward valuation operators stay adjoint.
reason: A derivation and admissibility argument with no captions, no tables and no figures. Nothing is calibrated or estimated; the order-book structure is a modelling assumption, not a dataset.

method: Reframes portfolio optimization around the one-dimensional gain probability density function, showing Markowitz, CVaR-deviation and higher-moment objectives are all functionals of it, and proposes directly matching a manager-specified target PDF plus a projected-gradient method to price the resulting sub-optimality in budget units.
reason: The numerical illustration uses a portfolio of energy-producing assets labelled generically as asset1, asset2, ... in Figure 2, with an ROI gain PDF produced by the authors' own statistical model. No identifiable traded instrument or public price history is used, so there is nothing to reproduce against free data.

method: Recasts look-ahead-freedom as temporal non-interference over a time-indexed information lattice, proves it undecidable (Pi-0-1-hard) when availability depends on data values, and gives a sound, linearly decidable type-and-effect system for the value-independent fragment covering windowing, resampling, joins, point-in-time reads and agentic retrieval, with a checker artifact.
reason: The paper states outright that its headline figures are computed from proprietary market data that cannot be redistributed, and that the public artifact reproduces the method and qualitative claims on synthetic data only. Table 1's real-data oracle validation is therefore not rerunnable from free sources; the rest is formal theory about pipelines rather than an empirical market claim.

method: Prices wind power purchase agreements under joint price and volumetric uncertainty by modelling electricity spot prices and wind speed as seasonal Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (Gaussian and jump-diffusion) processes, then computes CVA, DVA and BVA using CIR hazard rates calibrated to counterparty CDS.
reason: The credit-risk half, which is the paper's stated contribution, calibrates hazard rates to ENEL and ENI CDS spreads downloaded from Refinitiv Datastream, a paid feed. The underlying series are also outside the free list: Italian PUN electricity prices from GME and NASA POWER wind speeds are not market price data covered by any listed free source.
